message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the Harry Potter series; introduces Harry, Hogwarts, and the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second book; explores the mystery of the Chamber and the basilisk. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Tri‑wizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on the formation of Dumbledore’s Army. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s past and Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Final book; concludes the epic saga. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; a dark political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable released as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |
| **Cormoran Strike Series** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013–present | A detective series featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike and his assistant Robin Ellacott. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 | Companion book to the Harry Potter films; later adapted into its own film series. |

These titles represent the bulk of Rowling’s most widely read and celebrated works.
